title: Make task state store Execution API routes async
body:
related: #67799 This PR converts the four Execution API task state store routes to `async def` with `AsyncSessionDep`: * `GET /store/ti/{task_instance_id}/{key}` (`get_task_state_store`) * `PUT /store/ti/{task_instance_id}/{key}` (`set_task_state_store`) * `DELETE /store/ti/{task_instance_id}/{key}` (`delete_task_state_store`) * `DELETE /store/ti/{task_instance_id}` (`clear_task_state_store`) Details: * The routes call the configured backend's `aget` / `aset` / `adelete` / `aclear` with the route's session. These methods are abstract on `BaseStoreBackend`, so every backend already implements them. The state store docs already tell custom backends with a synchronous client to offload their async methods to a thread, and the `common.io` object-storage backend does so. * The task instance lookup selects the five columns it uses and filters on `working_set IS TRUE`. Before, `session.get(TI, ...)` loaded the full task instance and its joined Dag run. * `MetastoreBackend._aget_task_state_store` selects only `value` instead of the full row. The column is `NOT NULL`, so a missing key still returns `None`. * GET decodes the stored value and builds the response model in a worker thread (`run_in_threadpool`). Without this, a large value blocks the event loop longer than the synchronous route did (measurements below). The HTTP contract does not change, so no Execution API version change is needed.

Benchmarks and Testing

### Event-loop stall measurements The harness is adapted from the review of #74540. Each request runs over HTTP through `TestClient` from a separate thread. A 1 ms ticker on the server loop records its longest sleep per request. Every case asserts the status and the returned or stored value. 10 warm requests per case, cold request dropped, 2 rounds per version run interleaved in one container. GET/PUT values are integer arrays. Each cell shows `median / max` stall in ms for round 1; round 2. * **base**: the synchronous routes on `main`. * **head**: async routes without any offload. * **offload**: head plus offloading GET decoding/model building and PUT `json.dumps`. **This PR ships head for PUT/DELETE/CLEAR and offload for GET.** Python 3.14.8, SQLAlchemy 2.0.54, Breeze CI image. These are small local samples of event-loop availability, not throughput. **SQLite (aiosqlite)** | Request | Value | base | head | offload | |---|---:|---|---|---| | GET | 0.4 KB | 2 / 2; 2 / 3 | 3 / 4; 3 / 4 | 4 / 5; 3 / 4 | | GET | 58.9 KB | 14 / 17; 15 / 24 | 16 / 31; 14 / 31 | 16 / 28; 15 / 23 | | GET | 688.9 KB | 106 / 144; 119 / 200 | 144 / 217; 144 / 158 | 123 / 145; 102 / 139 | | PUT | 0.4 KB | 2 / 5; 3 / 6 | 3 / 6; 3 / 4 | 3 / 4; 3 / 5 | | PUT | 58.9 KB | 7 / 17; 9 / 17 | 11 / 15; 12 / 25 | 12 / 14; 12 / 25 | | PUT | 688.9 KB | 60 / 86; 81 / 159 | 89 / 109; 93 / 102 | 103 / 138; 100 / 119 | | DELETE | - | 2 / 3; 4 / 5 | 3 / 4; 4 / 4 | 4 / 8; 4 / 4 | | CLEAR, 1000 keys | - | 2 / 2; 2 / 3 | 3 / 4; 4 / 4 | 4 / 4; 4 / 4 | | CLEAR, 5000 keys | - | 2 / 3; 2 / 4 | 3 / 4; 3 / 3 | 3 / 4; 3 / 4 | **PostgreSQL (psycopg async)** | Request | Value | base | head | offload | |---|---:|---|---|---| | GET | 0.4 KB | 3 / 5; 3 / 4 | 5 / 5; 4 / 5 | 4 / 5; 4 / 5 | | GET | 58.9 KB | 19 / 27; 17 / 24 | 24 / 31; 21 / 27 | 19 / 27; 17 / 27 | | GET | 688.9 KB | 143 / 153; 147 / 155 | 206 / 256; 199 / 232 | 152 / 171; 127 / 153 | | PUT | 0.4 KB | 3 / 5; 3 / 4 | 4 / 4; 4 / 5 | 4 / 6; 4 / 6 | | PUT | 58.9 KB | 10 / 18; 12 / 16 | 18 / 25; 15 / 19 | 19 / 24; 18 / 20 | | PUT | 688.9 KB | 90 / 104; 86 / 95 | 133 / 161; 121 / 170 | 128 / 165; 125 / 138 | | DELETE | - | 3 / 4; 3 / 4 | 3 / 4; 4 / 6 | 4 / 4; 4 / 5 | | CLEAR, 1000 keys | - | 3 / 4; 3 / 4 | 4 / 5; 4 / 5 | 4 / 5; 3 / 5 | | CLEAR, 5000 keys | - | 3 / 5; 3 / 4 | 3 / 4; 4 / 6 | 4 / 5; 3 / 6 | Findings: * **GET**: without offload, the async route's median stall for a 689 KB value is 21–44% above base, depending on backend and round. With decoding and model building in a worker thread, GET is back at the base level on both backends. * **PUT is above base, and I found no remedy inside the route.** For a 689 KB value, the median stall is 15–78% above base, depending on backend and round. For a 59 KB value, it is 2–9 ms longer. Offloading `json.dumps` does not help (about 7 ms of the work). The loop-thread profiles show the same CPU on the loop in all three versions: three pydantic validations of the `JsonValue` body plus one cadwyn `model_dump`. The difference is where the loop gets a break. My reading of the code, which I have not instrumented directly: cadwyn's request migration re-runs FastAPI's `solve_dependencies`. With the synchronous `SessionDep`, that resolves the generator dependency through `contextmanager_in_threadpool`, which yields the loop in the middle of the framework work. `AsyncSessionDep` gives no such yield. A probe with `await asyncio.sleep(0)` at handler entry recovered only part of the gap (PostgreSQL, PUT only): | Value | base | head | head + yield | |---:|---|---|---| | 58.9 KB | 11 / 12; 10 / 15 | 18 / 26; 19 / 25 | 16 / 22; 16 / 26 | | 688.9 KB | 79 / 91; 101 / 120 | 141 / 172; 145 / 183 | 124 / 145; 134 / 165 | This cost belongs to framework request handling for large bodies and likely applies to any async Execution API route with a large `JsonValue` body. I left PUT without offload or yield, and I am raising it here for reviewers to decide. * **Small requests**: every route keeps the loop about 1 ms longer than base, because async SQLAlchemy work now runs on the loop instead of in a worker thread. Request duration is equal or lower. I did not measure stalls on MySQL. The contract tests ran there. ## Tests * The existing HTTP contract tests in `versions/head/test_task_state_store.py` pass unchanged. * `test_routes_select_columns_without_loading_entities` (all four routes) asserts that no ORM entity is loaded during the request. It fails on `main`, where `TaskInstance` and `DagRun` are loaded. Two negative controls confirm that it detects loads through `AsyncSession`: restoring the full-row value getter fails only the GET case, and restoring `session.get(TI, ...)` fails with `TaskInstance` and `DagRun`. * `test_get_builds_response_off_the_event_loop` asserts that the response model is built without a running event loop. It fails when the offload is removed from the async handler. It also passes on `main`, because the synchronous handler already ran in a worker thread. It guards the offload. Checks run: * `pytest` on `test_task_state_store.py` and `tests/unit/state/test_metastore.py`, in Breeze with Python 3.14.8: 107 passed on each backend: * SQLite (`sqlite` / `sqlite+aiosqlite`) * PostgreSQL (`postgresql+psycopg` / `postgresql+psycopg_async`) * MySQL (`mysql` / `mysql+aiomysql`) * `prek run mypy-airflow-core`: no issues. * `prek run --stage pre-commit` on the changed files: passed.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(

+def test_routes_select_columns_without_loading_entities(
+    client, create_task_instance, method, key, kwargs, expected_status
+):
+    ti = create_task_instance()
+    assert client.put(_api_url(ti.id, "job_id"), json={"value": "stored"}).status_code == 204
+    loaded = []
+
+    def record(_, instance):
+        loaded.append(type(instance).__name__)
+
+    event.listen(Session, "loaded_as_persistent", record)
+    try:
+        response = getattr(client, method)(_api_url(ti.id, key), **kwargs)
+    finally:
+        event.remove(Session, "loaded_as_persistent", record)
+
+    assert response.status_code == expected_status
+    assert loaded == []
+
